A two-day hangover ` [Highlight start] happens when hangover symptoms—like fatigue, brain fog, headache, nausea, and anxiety—last past 24 hours, often stretching 36 to 72 hours after heavy drinking [Highlight end] ` . While most hangovers fade within a day, lingering effects can happen due to severe dehydration, disrupted sleep, stomach irritation, inflammation, and slower alcohol metabolism.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXi9qOCIrfGqy59Wv9h3EUmmnx7QzhGcgilM_xQSCuZ4e-JYuaB_-6bHMD7AEaomi-HycbVT07UYUXQkEOznTAoFTQJxFnuKfhzrq_adPOnlplKzsuFL9AkgHUCgxG08So)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF14B1Tobbk1plajYMQ3e_eTts8AcrtB2jhdfyYqo5_99pcrAP5yAYXq-ldrqLvEV56hf4SN1EscQpnA_bDim1eujT1KVFFtr8IbaImqDCtXkCNkobg_YOFYtKxH1c3bqwXlWAbFzNeKpSZJjb4uUOsjKKrYrmlH3U7kSgw_dsfi_yOJ7rztPHxi1istw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_xhfCCHHLKetkEJbvP8gjs_ElizO33NPY0Dt2aNlalmdYhnQb0kxWQMkTqvf37uBPSjOHuPZgUrEasQUnsoei7ttYqvWPgjBHYlgsU4CsqFWued2lByrljgTpH4cORkc5benHHSj1UGxbdJBpMVUKIme8uJg5rDBH7cOOvjxmXg)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXX_v0j_sd9xUlwbpj9cNPU28aFv4iUvxIFde9Zuzlo340f6Jn5hX9Q7gQ_oxot_DcPcJIc5dCBB1nUQ1Ss4rIdFDQPf3vRKGaDGbAEmjcFtH31m0CNk48qR0mtc-bfIzIaFdRAwi6uBjCK-BEdMCwHB1lmxzf-orE)

### Why It Can Last Two Days

- **Heavy or consecutive drinking:** More alcohol means more toxic byproducts (like acetaldehyde) and a harder recovery.
- **Poor sleep:** Alcohol fragments sleep architecture, leaving deep fatigue that takes extra days to shake.
- **Stomach and immune strain:** Alcohol irritates the stomach lining and triggers body-wide inflammation.
- **Individual factors:** Age, genetics, medications (such as SSRIs), drinking on an empty stomach, and darker drinks high in congeners can lengthen recovery.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXX_v0j_sd9xUlwbpj9cNPU28aFv4iUvxIFde9Zuzlo340f6Jn5hX9Q7gQ_oxot_DcPcJIc5dCBB1nUQ1Ss4rIdFDQPf3vRKGaDGbAEmjcFtH31m0CNk48qR0mtc-bfIzIaFdRAwi6uBjCK-BEdMCwHB1lmxzf-orE)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXi9qOCIrfGqy59Wv9h3EUmmnx7QzhGcgilM_xQSCuZ4e-JYuaB_-6bHMD7AEaomi-HycbVT07UYUXQkEOznTAoFTQJxFnuKfhzrq_adPOnlplKzsuFL9AkgHUCgxG08So)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF14B1Tobbk1plajYMQ3e_eTts8AcrtB2jhdfyYqo5_99pcrAP5yAYXq-ldrqLvEV56hf4SN1EscQpnA_bDim1eujT1KVFFtr8IbaImqDCtXkCNkobg_YOFYtKxH1c3bqwXlWAbFzNeKpSZJjb4uUOsjKKrYrmlH3U7kSgw_dsfi_yOJ7rztPHxi1istw)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_xhfCCHHLKetkEJbvP8gjs_ElizO33NPY0Dt2aNlalmdYhnQb0kxWQMkTqvf37uBPSjOHuPZgUrEasQUnsoei7ttYqvWPgjBHYlgsU4CsqFWued2lByrljgTpH4cORkc5benHHSj1UGxbdJBpMVUKIme8uJg5rDBH7cOOvjxmXg)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjQEBxCJF1-gNectD5L0hhcujKhTli3IqOtHlEX-mux0uVkYL9Qkm2OIWJt3R2phhLtyslnjdaz4PCk2W5gZ73xYcP8x3MRVmjUapYBKo5j-6xh6m-b9vDWth3UD6eS1h5WD0BVqDKD4tLS_f7cwtiLaqicCifRedb3FwrnuL5xHXzFlagm-OpEBlSiIgzf0)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXX5NdFb-NOjhQDfGiupaZSIfG12emDqk6CtB-ShWoETZ3rQhACmXOB_cBShuG0EmuMR8LiuqlrNzEjgMjYgOnwKHzMat14ATlLUDEFXyCtSbS0YQ0RAen6MHR4B11KPgBdxBPMxD6b)

### What Helps You Recover

- **Rehydrate steadily:** Sip water, broth, or electrolyte fluids throughout the day. (For mobile hangover IV options, see [Pure IV](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXi9qOCIrfGqy59Wv9h3EUmmnx7QzhGcgilM_xQSCuZ4e-JYuaB_-6bHMD7AEaomi-HycbVT07UYUXQkEOznTAoFTQJxFnuKfhzrq_adPOnlplKzsuFL9AkgHUCgxG08So).)
- **Eat gentle foods:** Try plain carbs, eggs, bananas, or broth when your stomach settles.
- **Prioritize rest:** Give your body time and sleep to recover.
- **Be cautious with medications:** Avoid mixing acetaminophen with alcohol due to liver strain, and use NSAIDs like ibuprofen carefully if your stomach is irritated. Skip "hair of the dog" alcohol, which only prolongs symptoms.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_xhfCCHHLKetkEJbvP8gjs_ElizO33NPY0Dt2aNlalmdYhnQb0kxWQMkTqvf37uBPSjOHuPZgUrEasQUnsoei7ttYqvWPgjBHYlgsU4CsqFWued2lByrljgTpH4cORkc5benHHSj1UGxbdJBpMVUKIme8uJg5rDBH7cOOvjxmXg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXMWi5Ho6mceUr7moM7-Njp0hetpq11aQqXJXoomUhmO4k4ZcX2wtaUoSTI205eb_AIEOWDBHYRhcMJs9XROG2bqFIF8WQiD4nZACQFPsHydFkQs9spqBOI4oi4HRm1BShHnW43Ww_aTAaWFUT0r4BMVICpA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXn-ZYAcAG8mwRii1VpgQQog7CFJVUpKweGD7bT51lEms8zNnJkmVJ071HYZRa4lHfg3lFIPYFNqiRztEiDtx2E4F4aTI8B4-fRBcjq38o_EeXJDUicgi0mcsuD5XNO1OfIw)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXi9qOCIrfGqy59Wv9h3EUmmnx7QzhGcgilM_xQSCuZ4e-JYuaB_-6bHMD7AEaomi-HycbVT07UYUXQkEOznTAoFTQJxFnuKfhzrq_adPOnlplKzsuFL9AkgHUCgxG08So)

### When to Seek Care
If you drink frequently and experience severe tremors, heavy sweating, racing heartbeat, confusion, or worsening symptoms rather than a gradual fade, it could be alcohol withdrawal—which requires prompt medical evaluation. Seek care right away if you cannot keep fluids down or have severe abdominal pain or chest symptoms.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqAEBxCJF13PF7jv9DteNos4EA087e-6uBwhhJe2GH0oxdh0ikeEVhkPRlVGg3xzGts5sS0EoaJD6YoYIMGGjSyWCAzkxF6nwfVHX4p2SQZ4dOrDDqht97v5yHaSlMDD0v2oIpHfh_fdtS_cZjK_pczACvvPOouffzdzmJNdN_MEItbW_HCIVFcGhCT1gyG4xaBsEoonHETpGUS8b8GczJQRMj6XBeejvwxY)Are you trying to recover from one right now, or looking into **why yours last so long** ? Sharing your **main symptoms** or **how much you typically drink** can help tailor this further.
